_comment: Each Secure by Design control against the ASVS 5.0 requirements that ask the same thing, chosen by reading both texts on 25 September 2026. The checklist has no levels of its own; sv derives one from its critical flag and severityIfNo. Through this file a control's level becomes the lower of that and the lowest level among its ASVS counterparts, so a crosswalk entry can bring a control in sooner and never hide one. A control with no counterpart (an empty list: nothing in ASVS asks the same thing) is shown at every target level, because dropping it would rest on sv's own invention alone. Evidence about a counterpart is shown beside the control as supporting, never as checking it. Each counterpart carries a few words naming what the two ask in common, and the citation guard requires those words to share vocabulary with both texts: the checklist's statements are too terse for a direct comparison (`TLS` is shorter than the guard's shortest word), and a bridge that must agree with both sides is a stricter test than either side alone. Every control must be listed, empty or not, so a new one cannot default silently; every citation is held to the same vocabulary guard as the rest (crates/sv-check/tests/citations.rs).

SBD-AS-07.V16.5.2: services keep operating securely when a dependency they access fails, handled with fallback patterns

SBD-DM-01.V14.1.2: each data classification has documented protection controls

SBD-DM-02.V12.2.1: encryption in transit with TLS for every client connection
SBD-DM-02.V12.3.1: encryption in transit with TLS for every inbound and outbound connection

SBD-DM-04.V2.3.3: transactions that either succeed entirely or are rolled back

SBD-DM-05.V14.1.2: retention requirements defined for each data class
SBD-DM-05.V14.2.7: retention classification that deletes outdated data

SBD-RR-01.V16.5.1: safe error handling that exposes nothing when an exception occurs
SBD-RR-01.V16.5.3: safe error handling that fails securely when an exception occurs

SBD-RR-02.V16.5.2: circuit breakers and graceful degradation when a dependency fails

SBD-RR-05.V2.3.4: locking and concurrency controls against double-booking

SBD-RR-06.V13.2.6: timeouts and retry strategies on every connection to other services
SBD-RR-06.V13.1.3: timeouts and failure handling defined for every external service

SBD-RR-07.V2.4.1: rate limits and quotas against excessive calls

SBD-AC-01.V12.3.1: all communications encrypted with TLS on every connection
SBD-AC-01.V12.3.3: all communications between internal services encrypted with TLS
SBD-AC-01.V12.3.4: service identity verified with trusted certificates between internal services
SBD-AC-01.V12.3.5: service identity verified with strong authentication, such as TLS client certificates, between services

SBD-AC-03.V8.1.1: access rules that apply least privilege by permissions and attributes
SBD-AC-03.V8.2.1: access restricted to explicit permissions, least privilege

SBD-AC-04.V8.3.1: authorization enforced centrally at a trusted service layer

SBD-AC-05.V13.3.1: secrets kept in a secret manager or key vault
SBD-AC-05.V13.3.4: secrets that expire and are rotated

SBD-MT-01.V16.1.1: logs with a documented structure, formats and storage
SBD-MT-01.V16.2.1: log entries carrying the metadata needed to trace an event
SBD-MT-01.V16.4.3: logs sent to a separate, centralized system

SBD-MT-07.V16.4.2: audit logs protected so they cannot be modified, tamper-evident
